thread.title_full: Report: 87% of students at Huffman ISD schools not on college track in 2024-25 school year

author: W. P. Parson
title: Report: 87% of students at Huffman ISD schools not on college track in 2024-25 school year
text:
Of the 3,638 students in Huffman ISD’s schools, 3,166 (87%) were not on track for college in the 2024-25 school year, according to East Houston News’ analysis of STAAR scores from the Texas Education Agency (TEA) .
The TEA considers students to be on track for college if they demonstrate mastery of the course content through the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR).
In the 2023-24 school year, the TEA noted that 3,198 students at Huffman ISD—equivalent to 87% of the student population—were not on the academic path to college eligibility. This continued with the 2024-25 school year, where the percentage also stood at 87%.
Data shows that two of Huffman ISD’s 10 American Indian students, 20% (17) of its 87 multiracial students, one of its six Pacific Islander students, 15% (337) of its 2,253 white students, 11% (15) of its 144 African American students, 9% (100) of its 1,120 Hispanic students, and 6% (1) of its 18 Asian students had mastered their grade level in the 2024-25 school year and were “on track for college and career readiness,” as measured by state academic standards .
For the past two years, from 2023-24 to the 2024-25 school year, none of Huffman ISD’s Asian students have met the college readiness benchmark in Mathematics or Reading.
Primary data on overall student readiness in Huffman ISD is derived from the TSI assessments, which evaluate student capabilities in reading, writing, and mathematics. Certain students may qualify for exemptions from these assessments.
A 2026 study by WalletHub classified Texas as one of the least-educated states in the U.S. , ranking it 41st out of 50 in educational quality and student outcomes.
Texas has the nation’s second-largest K-12 public school system , serving about 5.5 million students with a student-to-teacher ratio of roughly 15:1.
